paper_metadata.title: The maximum-likelihood quantum amplitude estimation algorithm provides the best tradeoff between accuracy and circuit depth among quantum solutions for integral estimation

summary: The paper benchmarks three gate-based quantum amplitude estimation variants on a 1D integral of sin^2(x): standard QAE, maximum-likelihood QAE (MLQAE), and iterative QAE (IQAE), all simulated on 3 qubits with Qiskit Aer. The reported empirical slopes are approximately -1.267 ± 0.206 for standard QAE, -0.974 ± 0.058 for MLQAE, -0.971 ± 0.092 for IQAE, and -0.485 ± 0.051 for classical Metropolis-Hastings Monte Carlo, with MLQAE described as the best trade-off between circuit depth and precision but without a demonstrated practical quantum advantage over classical methods.

experiments.description: Standard quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) benchmark for 1D integral estimation of sin^2(x) using a 3-qubit Qiskit Aer simulator implementation.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Uniform distribution over n qubits with an ancilla qubit; P prepares equal superposition over x and R encodes sin((x+1/2)bmax/2^n) via controlled-Y rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate I = (1/bmax) * integral_0^{bmax} sin^2(x) dx via amplitude estimation of a = E_p[g(x)]

problem_instance.description: 1D numerical integration benchmark using the function sin^2(x).
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Integral discretized as D = sum_{x=0}^{2^n-1} (1/2^n) sin^2((x+1/2)bmax/2^n).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Average of 10 executions with different simulator seeds; error vs number of samples/oracle queries and circuit depth reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize integral on n qubits; prepare uniform superposition and controlled rotations for function encoding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Estimate amplitude from measured ancilla outcomes; convert to integral estimate.

speedup_claims.conditions: ideal QAE with M oracle queries; fault-tolerant setting
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that current hardware is not suitable for the standard phase-estimation-based QAE; practical advantage is not shown on hardware.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/M) in estimation error with M oracle queries

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large fault-tolerant quantum hardware with low error rates; standard QAE needs phase estimation, controlled powers of Q, and QFT, plus many repetitions for reliability.
limiting_factors: Only local Qiskit Aer simulation on a 3-qubit toy integral
Standard QAE requires deep phase-estimation-style circuits
Classical Monte Carlo baseline is used only for comparison

notes: Circuit depth for the standard QAE benchmark is discussed qualitatively and in Figure 1, but no single numeric depth value is explicitly stated in the text excerpt.
Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper explicitly says all simulations were performed on the Qiskit Aer local simulator.
The paper reports quadratic scaling in theory, but does not demonstrate practical advantage on hardware.
The benchmark is a simulator-only toy problem.

experiments.description: Maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation (MLAE / MLQAE) benchmark for the same 1D sin^2(x) integral using a 3-qubit Qiskit Aer simulator implementation.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same 3-qubit discretized integral encoding as the standard QAE benchmark; Grover-like circuits with repeated Q applications and ancilla measurement.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate I = (1/bmax) * integral_0^{bmax} sin^2(x) dx by maximum-likelihood estimation of amplitude a = sin^2(theta_a)

problem_instance.description: 1D numerical integration benchmark using the function sin^2(x).
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Integral discretized as D = sum_{x=0}^{2^n-1} (1/2^n) sin^2((x+1/2)bmax/2^n).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Average of 10 executions with different simulator seeds; 100 shots per quantum circuit; error vs number of samples/oracle queries and circuit depth reported.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Maximum likelihood estimation; Metropolis-Hastings Monte Carlo (baseline)
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize integral on n qubits; prepare uniform superposition and controlled rotations for function encoding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Maximum-likelihood fit over theta_a; convert ˆtheta_a to ˆa = sin^2(ˆtheta_a) and then to integral estimate.

speedup_claims.conditions: empirical scaling on the 1D sin^2(x) benchmark with 3 qubits and 100 shots per circuit
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states MLQAE is less than quadratic in theory in one place, but the fitted slope is close to -1 and the authors describe it as comparable to QAE and better than classical Monte Carlo.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Less than quadratic advantage reported; empirical scaling slope approximately -0.974 ± 0.058 in error vs samples

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Shallow Grover-like circuits plus classical MLE, but still requires quantum circuit execution and repeated shots; advantage would require larger problem sizes and hardware beyond simulator.
limiting_factors: No direct classical-vs-quantum runtime advantage demonstrated
Paper reports only empirical scaling on a toy integral
Classical Monte Carlo remains the baseline

notes: The paper reports 100 shots per quantum circuit for MLQAE and 10 independent simulator seeds.
Circuit depth is discussed comparatively in Figure 1, but no single numeric depth value is explicitly stated in the text excerpt.
The paper states MLQAE is the fastest among the tested quantum methods in the simulator, but this is not a demonstrated practical quantum advantage over classical methods.

experiments.description: Iterative quantum amplitude estimation (IQAE) benchmark for the same 1D sin^2(x) integral using a 3-qubit Qiskit Aer simulator implementation.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: target accuracy epsilon and confidence level 1-alpha
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start with confidence interval [0, pi/2] and k0 = 0.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same 3-qubit discretized integral encoding as the standard QAE benchmark; repeated Q^k A circuits with ancilla measurement.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate I = (1/bmax) * integral_0^{bmax} sin^2(x) dx by iterative refinement of the amplitude estimate

problem_instance.description: 1D numerical integration benchmark using the function sin^2(x).
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Integral discretized as D = sum_{x=0}^{2^n-1} (1/2^n) sin^2((x+1/2)bmax/2^n).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Average of 10 executions with different simulator seeds; 100 shots per quantum circuit; 90% confidence interval used for IQAE.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical iterative routine (FindNextK) and Metropolis-Hastings Monte Carlo baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize integral on n qubits; prepare uniform superposition and controlled rotations for function encoding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Update confidence interval from measured amplitudes; invert relation a = cos((4k+2)theta_a) to refine estimate.

speedup_claims.conditions: iterative amplitude estimation with target accuracy epsilon and confidence level 1-alpha
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the iterative method achieves quadratic speedup up to a factor depending on Nmax and confidence level; empirical slope is close to -1.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic speedup over Monte Carlo with iteration count T = ceil(log2(pi/(8 epsilon)))

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Shallow iterative Grover-like circuits with classical control logic; still requires repeated quantum sampling and is evaluated only in simulation.
limiting_factors: No practical advantage over classical methods demonstrated
Performance depends on classical FindNextK routine and repeated circuit executions
Classical Monte Carlo baseline remains the reference

notes: The paper reports 100 shots per quantum circuit and 10 independent simulator seeds for IQAE.
Circuit depth is discussed comparatively in Figure 1, but no single numeric depth value is explicitly stated in the text excerpt.
The paper reports IQAE as competitive with MLQAE in scaling, but not as a practical quantum advantage over classical Monte Carlo.
